John Hennessey Drives the Most Powerful Truck With a Combustion Engine, Ram 1500 TRX
12 photos
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube
Hypercar builder John Hennessey got his hands on a truck with nearly hypercar performance figures. He took the all-new Ram 1500 SRT TRX, just fresh out the factory, for a spin on the track to see what it can do before he works his magic on the already monstrous contraption.
At the Pennzoil Proving Grounds at Lonestar Motorsports Park, in Sealy, Texas, he puts the all-new Ram 1500 SRT TRX through its paces. It has just arrived from the factory, and its stock days are numbered. It will get the Mammoth 1000 pack, along with some other special treats, John Hennessey reveals.
But before it undergoes transformation, John Hennessey wants to see how it compares to the previous TRX. The moment he presses the throttle, he goes, " Oh, yeah! " The transmission shifts firmly, the HEMI orchestra roars out its drama out back, and the truck seems ready to bite big chunks off the pavement.
However, even though the Ram truck looks and acts like a ferocious beast, it still makes a great and reliable daily driver. " In Texas, everybody drives a pickup truck ," says the performance guru. But not everyone drives a truck that stands out even before any aftermarket upgrade.
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube He says the Ford F-150 Raptor R feels lighter, and the aluminum body has something to do with it. It is not just a feeling, but reality. A fully optioned F-150 Raptor R tips the scales at 6,090 pounds (2,762 kilograms), while the SRT TRX weighs 6,750 pounds (3,062 kilograms). That is a solid 660-pound (299-kilogram) weight gap between the two.
However, the TRX compensates with the extra power. The 6.2-liter supercharged HEMI V8 pumps out 777 horsepower (788 metric horsepower) and 680 pound-feet (922 Newton meters) of torque for a run from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 3.5 seconds, a quarter mile in 12.2 seconds, and a top speed of 118 mph (190 kph).
In the meantime, the Raptor R has to deal with the 5.2-liter supercharged Carnivore V8, which churns out 720 horsepower (730 metric horsepower) and 640 pound-feet (868 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 in 3.6 seconds, run the quarter mile in 12.1 seconds, and max out at 114 mph (184 kph).
The extra weight by no means feels like a drawback. It might actually work in its favor, as John Hennessey says it feels more planted, with no compromise whatsoever on the fun factor. He congratulates Tim Kuniskis , the man who returned to Stellantis after a short-lived retirement, following former CEO Carlos Tavares’s abrupt departure, to fix the mistakes of the previous management.
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube Tim Kuniskis is the man who brought back the HEMI, along with the TRX, in the Ram 1500 lineup, giving the Ford F-150 Raptor R a run for its money once again. The all-new SRT TRX is a monster from the moment it rolls off the production line.
However, Hennessey's Mammoth package is going to turn it into a drag strip and desert weapon , making it the first TRX dialed up by the Texas-based tuner after the return of the HEMI V8. And it will, indeed, rolling weapon with very reliable track capabilities, unless Hennessey Performance decides to slam it for enhanced hypercar behavior.
The upgrade brings a high-flow supercharger system, upgraded front and rear drive pulleys, a heavy-duty supercharger belt, and a crank damper pin assembly. High-flow fuel injectors, a performance air induction system, upgraded spark plugs, a revised crankcase ventilation system, a cooler thermostat, and custom engine (ECM) and transmission (TCM) calibrations will also be part of the plan.
All these mods will most likely drop the 0 to 60 time to 3.2 seconds and the quarter-mile time to just 11.4 seconds, with a trap speed of 120 mph (193 kph), because that is what the Hennessey Performance experts do for a living.
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube Hennessey is keeping busy at this time of year. The tuning experts have recently delivered a VelociRaptoR to NASCAR driver Joey Logano . The truck was officially dialed up to 1,000 horsepower. The 5.2-liter supercharged V8 now makes 1,200 horsepower at the wheel.
In the meantime, Hennessey Performance is working around the clock to fine-tune the Blackbird, its all-new in-house-developed supercar and the first since the Venom F5. While the most powerful Venom came with 2,031 horsepower and a manual transmission, the Blackbird is more tamed in a fun way.
Hennessey’s upcoming model is an aerospace-inspired (no, it won’t fly and it won’t flip mid-air like the Tesla Roadster) hypercar with zero screens and analog everything. It is powered by an Ilmor-developed 6.2-liter naturally aspirated V8 that revs past 9,000 rpm and puts out 850 horsepower.
The Blackbird is Hennessey’s only second model built from the ground up after the Venom F5, unveiled back in 2020. The Venom GT doesn't count.
